idiom_name: vi.spyOn/jest.spyOn with typed keyof, or a subclass with override
implementation_notes: TypeScript keeps JavaScript's runtime story - patch the method with vi.spyOn(obj, 'now') / jest.spyOn(...), restored through vi.restoreAllMocks() - and adds compile-time safety: the spy key must be a real member (K extends keyof T) and the mock must satisfy the member's type, so the classic typo'd-override and wrong-signature failure modes are caught by the type checker. When a real subclass is wanted (for example because the instance is created inside the SUT), class SutTss extends Sut with the override modifier keeps the same check (TypeScript 4.3+), and private/# private members are simply out of reach for both routes.
pitfalls: Spying through a class constructor patches the prototype and is process-global: without restoreMocks: true (or an explicit restoreAllMocks) other tests in the same worker see the stub.
private/#private members cannot be spied with the two-argument form - # fields are not properties at all - and getters need the accessor form vi.spyOn(obj, 'prop', 'get') or a real double.
In Vitest Browser Mode you cannot spy directly on exported methods; the documented workaround, vi.mock(path, { spy: true }), changes how the module is loaded and affects every importer.
